I’m dual hatted. I am an engineering supervisor and I also still have to do engineering work as a product owner. I recently have had the privilege to scoop up some incredible software developers who’d been laid off from other companies rash decision to downsize their developers because their leadership clearly hasn’t actually played around with AI… instead the leadership of said companies purchased AI tools and got hyped up on claims that they could slash their “overpriced engineers”… Their reluctance to embrace and play around with AI was my direct gain as a manager and product owner. since adopting AI we have been able to explode our coding productivity. As a PO I found myself having to augment the team just to keep the teams deliveries on time. There simply were not enough of us because we are now able to produce so much more code in a given sprint, and as a supervisor I kept hearing the same thing from all my directs. “There is just too much to do.” Software developers are producing more code thanks to AI, as a result, we are, producing more artifacts to review, more features to debug, more things to trouble shoot, and integrate, and there is more to package and deliver to the edge. The one thing we are doing less of is writing the code it’s self, so AI made producing code easier but as a result we are producing 80% more and then we still have to preform all the same functions on that extra workload. Im the busiest I’ve ever been im my career. I am routinely having to pull all nighters just to keep up…. Sooo 100% concur with this video. AI is creating an explosion in productivity and demand for labor. Ps if you are a good dev and you like to debug, automate, and troubleshoot, and above all LOVE integration, I’m hiring 🤗. I can promise you I am too busy to micromanage you or ensure you are following all the tiny company policies. I disagree with these points: 1. Can't code on front of people. A variety of people have a variety of personalities and comfort zones. If I can produce code that is very good, quality and efficient but operate poorly under peering eyes and pressure of being in the spotlight, you cannot write me off as a person who can't do the job. I'm not going to be in public competitions where I'm in the public eye, writing code on stage like it's a performance. As long as you can write good code and explain it, it goes a long way 2. Doing coding challenges. While this is not necessarily a disagreement, I'd say its not an objective truth. This is because it's just a skill that can just get you through an interview and maybe not end up facing coding challenges like those in the coding websites on the job. Yes they are good practice, but it is not objectively a tool to use to assess if you are ready to get a programming job. Some can challenge themselves by building projects all the time and never having to visit a coding challenge site. Again, if you can code, build something and explain it, that should go a long way.

As an actuary I can tell you about it a bit more specifically. So it is a really hard major (I think the hardest or the second hardest after theoretical physics ) , you can pass the tests if you try enough and expect failing, salary that’s presented in the video is not very representative of what I’ve had or what people have had , so you start with 75-80 k according to my experience, without passing the exams yet. The maths that is really used in actuary is probabilities and not statistics. Another thing is flexibility, I do think our education is really flexible (at the same time specific on various elements) from my experience, actuaries tend to be better in general maths than mathematicians (I don’t know why ) in fact I have many friends who quit actuary to join maths (because actuary is really hard ) and get A s in maths while we got c’s in actuary so I do think maths is fairly easier in comparison to ACT. Another thing , I don’t think that an actuary would ever be in a position of telling a programmer what to do or provide him with an algorithm so the programmer code it as actuaries are usually strong in coding themselves and we build our own AI’s (my masters were in AI) that are basically gonna replace us in the far future
